theme: 3 terms on deeper closures: closures that run later, closures that run right away and closures Swift writes for you

terms.definition: A closure that a function keeps and calls later, after the function has returned.
terms.example: Mark the completion handler as escaping, because we call it after the request finishes.

terms.definition: A closure that a function calls before it returns, which is the default in Swift.
terms.example: This closure is non-escaping, so you don't need to write self inside it.

terms.definition: A closure that Swift makes automatically from an expression you pass as an argument.
terms.example: The assert message uses an autoclosure, so Swift only builds the string if the check fails.

Today's terms
Escaping Closure - A closure that a function keeps and calls later, after the function has returned.
Non-Escaping Closure - A closure that a function calls before it returns, which is the default in Swift.
Autoclosure - A closure that Swift makes automatically from an expression you pass as an argument.

dialogue.title: Closures that run later

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, `fetch` gives me an error when I store `done` in `handlers`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's because `done` runs later. It has to be an Escaping Closure.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So I just add the escaping mark before the type?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. An Escaping Closure can still run after `fetch` returns.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then should I mark the `forEach` closure too?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No, that one runs right away. It's a Non-Escaping Closure.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wait, I thought every closure was escaping by default.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's the opposite. A closure parameter is a Non-Escaping Closure unless you mark it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. What about `check`? I pass `items.count > 2` without braces.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's an Autoclosure. Swift wraps the expression in a closure for you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice, so an Autoclosure only runs when `check` calls `ok`.
Store the handler for later? Mark it as an escaping closure.
